# Chapter 11: The Present

Bob can focus on the present now — the actual present, the only time any of us ever truly inhabit.

The morning begins with coffee alongside Cindy. Two people, two cups, the quiet exchange of company that decades of partnership have made second nature. The coffee itself matters less than what it represents: a daily commitment to showing up for one another, to the small maintenance that keeps a marriage alive across the years.
